title: n8n Workflow Automation
positioning: A workflow automation platform for technical teams that need visual workflows, code, integrations, AI steps, and a choice between managed cloud and self-hosting.
decisionAngles: Workflow execution billing versus provider and AI costs
Community versus paid collaboration, governance, and environment features
Source-available license boundaries for embedded or resale use
Queue-mode scaling, secrets, retries, observability, and binary-data handling

pricingSnapshot.billingUnit: One complete workflow run counts as one execution regardless of its number of steps; chat workloads can consume an execution for each message-triggered run.
plans: Starter: EUR 20/month billed annually, 2,500 workflow executions
Pro: EUR 50/month billed annually, 10,000 workflow executions
Business: EUR 667/month billed annually, 40,000 workflow executions and self-hosted collaboration/governance features
Enterprise: custom pricing for cloud or self-hosted deployments
volatileFields: AI Workflow Builder and AI Assistant credit allowances
pricingSnapshot.releaseGuard: Recheck the live pricing page immediately before migration; do not hard-code AI-credit allowances without a same-day verification.

licenseBoundary.label: Source-available fair-code under the Sustainable Use License, not OSI open source
licenseBoundary.allowedSummary: Free internal business, personal, and non-commercial use is generally allowed; paid consulting and support around customer-owned n8n workflows are allowed.
licenseBoundary.restrictedSummary: Hosting n8n and charging users for access, or selling a product whose value derives substantially from n8n, can require a separate commercial agreement.
licenseBoundary.releaseGuard: Never describe n8n as MIT, Apache-2.0, or unrestricted open source.

limitations: Self-hosting transfers upgrades, backups, database availability, Redis, worker health, encryption-key consistency, credential security, and monitoring to the operator.
Community edition omits projects, workflow and credential sharing, SSO, environments, external secrets, external binary storage, log streaming, multi-main mode, and Git version control.
Queue mode uses Redis plus a shared database; distributed queue mode over SQLite is unsupported, and filesystem binary storage is not supported for queue-mode persistence.
AI nodes and agents can require separate model-provider accounts, API charges, data-policy review, human approval, and output guardrails.
An execution quota can be consumed quickly by high-frequency schedules, retries, webhook events, or message-by-message chatbot workflows.
Source availability and self-hosting do not remove the Sustainable Use License restrictions on resale, hosted access, or embedded commercial products.

marketValidation.rationale: n8n has durable product, community, funding, release, and independent-review signals. Its strongest differentiator is combining visual workflow construction, code-level control, broad integrations, AI steps, and deployment choice. The recommendation must remain conditional because operating a production self-hosted instance and governing complex automations require engineering ownership.

recurringUserFriction: Steep learning curve for users without coding or API familiarity
